items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I want to mention a couple of recordings to you and see if they have any significance: Wilbert Harrison’s recording of “Kansas City.”

ctx.x: early stages, because you never get the innocence again and you never get the reach again. Once they’re successful they’re not at that place anymore. So the first albums are what I dig the most.
I want to mention a couple of recordings to you and see if they have any significance: Wilbert Harrison’s recording of “Kansas City.”

“Kansas City.” Liked it, you know, not one of my — I mean it’s not a record that I go back to but remember, first of all, I was in junior high or maybe the first year of high school so it was a big record. And Mike and Jerry you know, wrote it, so I always had a sentimental thing about that.
